title: Windows: managed app-server 0.159 persists after npm CLI downgrade and console popups continue

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

body:
### Summary

On Windows 11, visible CMD/PowerShell windows repeatedly appear in front of the desktop while I use the Codex CLI inside a PowerShell terminal in VS Code. The rate can reach dozens of windows in a short period, interrupting typing and making the CLI impractical to use. I downgraded the global npm CLI from 0.159.0 to 0.156.1, but a separately installed managed app-server daemon remained running from a 0.159.0 release path. The user-visible popup problem continued after the npm downgrade.

This report focuses on the mixed-version state and the fact that npm CLI downgrade does not stop or downgrade the managed daemon. The daemon-side console spawning problem is also described in #44768; related popup reports include #48074 and #48876.

### Environment

- Windows 11 Home, x64, build 26200.
- Codex CLI launched inside VS Code's integrated PowerShell terminal.
- Global npm package and `codex --version` after downgrade: `@openai/codex@0.156.1` / `codex-cli 0.156.1`.
- Managed daemon processes still ran from `~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/0.159.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/bin/codex.exe`:
  - `app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon`
  - `app-server daemon pid-update-loop`
- `~/.codex/config.toml` has no `[windows]` block. I also found no project `config.toml` override.

### What happened

1. I used Codex CLI on Windows after updating to 0.159.0 and saw repeated foreground console windows during normal agent work.
2. I removed the `[windows]` settings from my config; the popups continued.
3. I installed `@openai/codex@0.156.1` globally. `npm ls -g` and `codex --version` both confirmed 0.156.1 on disk, but the popup problem was still reported.
4. Process inspection found the two managed app-server processes above still running from the separate 0.159.0 release path. They were stopped explicitly; neither had restarted five seconds later.

Several CLI sessions started before the downgrade were also still running, so I cannot attribute every popup after the downgrade to the daemon or claim that a fresh 0.156.1-only session reproduces this. A newly started CLI process was present as well. I did not capture the parent process of each transient popup. The process/version mismatch is verified; the precise source of every visible window is not.

### Expected behavior

Background tool and daemon processes should not open foreground console windows. Downgrading or changing the CLI version should not leave an incompatible or problematic managed daemon silently serving CLI sessions; the CLI should handle that state clearly or provide a reliable automatic restart/version alignment path.

### Actual behavior and impact

The popup storm continued while `codex --version` showed 0.156.1 and the managed app-server still ran 0.159.0. The foreground window storm makes current Codex CLI releases unusable for my work in VS Code. I am stuck on 0.156.1 and unable to upgrade until this is fixed. This now blocks normal access to GPT-6.1 Sol, which was added to the bundled catalog in the 0.159.1 release.

### Requested investigation

Please confirm whether a CLI at 0.156.1 can attach to a 0.159.0 managed daemon, make daemon version/state visible in CLI diagnostics, and prevent visible Windows console creation for daemon-launched commands and helpers. A supported command that safely stops or aligns a stale daemon after npm upgrade/downgrade would also help.
